What is an AI "brain" - and how STA is building one

A plain-language look at where our AI knowledge lives, and where it's headed  ·  Updated 2026-07-06

Optional reading · No action needed

The short version: a "brain" is the shared pile of company knowledge an AI assistant reads so it actually knows School Tech - our products, processes, and answers - instead of guessing. We already have a working support brain, and we're now collecting the workflows that will feed a company-wide main brain - one every staff assistant draws from, kept in one place so a single update reaches everyone at once.

What "brain" actually means

An AI assistant on its own is smart but generic - it doesn't know our products, our customers, or how we do things. A brain fixes that. It's a curated set of company documents (product references, troubleshooting guides, the company profile, how-tos) that the assistant reads before it answers. Give it the brain and it stops guessing about School Tech and starts answering from our real knowledge.

Think of it like a company handbook the assistant has memorized and never forgets - except instead of one binder on a shelf, it's a living library the assistant checks every time you ask it something about STA.

Why it's worth building well:

  • Accuracy - answers come from current company docs, not a stale guess.
  • Consistency - every assistant that reads the same brain gives the same answer.
  • Less busywork - update knowledge in one place instead of re-teaching every assistant separately.

The catch we're solving

Right now, when we hand out an assistant it carries its own frozen copy of company knowledge. When a product doc changes, every copy is out of date until someone re-loads it - for every assistant, every time. Five assistants means five update chores. That gets worse with every new person, which is backwards. The fix is to keep the knowledge in one shared place that every assistant reads live.

How we get there - now, next, later

We're building this in stages, and each stage is useful on its own. No hard dates - the pace follows the company-server approval that the shared brain rides on.

Now - gathering the raw material

Collect the knowledge + stand up the server

Two things are happening now. First, we're collecting everyone's workflows - Tanya is coordinating the department-operations questionnaires that capture how each team actually works. Those answers become the raw material the brain is built from. Second, the company server that the shared brain will live on is being set up (targeting the end of this month). The support team's Support Chat already shows what a well-fed brain does for real work.

Next - get everyone using AI

First shared Cowork assistant

As the workflows come in, the focus shifts to getting staff comfortable using AI - the Claude Projects and tools we already have. The Work Assistant (a Cowork assistant) is currently Adam-only. The staff version - a stripped-down template for Chris and Tyler - is deferred, with no date set. Adam using it day to day still feeds real knowledge and workflow detail back into the system, which is what the later staff rollout would be built on.

Later - the shared brain

One company-wide brain, department brains on top

The collected workflows and shared knowledge consolidate into a company-wide main brain hosted on the server. Department brains (support, sales, and others) extend it with their own specialist knowledge. Because it's all in one place, a single edit updates every assistant instantly - update a product doc once, and every assistant at STA knows it that second.

Sequence: collect workflows + build the server (now) → get everyone using AI (next) → consolidate into a shared main brain with department brains on top (later). The Work Assistant stays Adam-only for now; a staff template strip is deferred with no date. Stages ship value as they land; timing tracks workflow collection and the server build.

What this means for you

  • The assistants you use will increasingly know STA - fewer confidently-wrong answers about our own products.
  • When company knowledge changes, it updates centrally - nothing for you to reinstall.
  • Nothing to do right now. This is background on where the AI program is headed. Ideas for what your team's brain should know are always welcome - bring them to the IT team or the AI Advisor.
